targetAudience.primary: Architects and reliability engineers building durable agent runtimes, task queues and multi-process workers
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands persisted queues, runtime resume and basic asynchronous retry patterns.
targetAudience.readerProblem: Persisted work can survive in storage yet remain dormant because the live runtime has no mechanism to notice cross-process changes or retry a blocked wake without stalling unrelated work.

whyNow: A same-day merged Codex change shows a concrete SQLite-backed reconciliation design using a coarse external-change signal, durable per-thread revisions, lifecycle reconciliation and independent per-thread retries.

externalHook.description: A task can be durable enough to survive a process and still be invisible to the process that is supposed to resume it.

coreProposition: Durable agent work should separate persistence from reconciliation: stored state needs external-change detection, durable object-level change identity, lifecycle reconciliation and isolated retry ownership before a live runtime can reliably rediscover and attempt progress.

originalValue.description: Turns one queue-watcher implementation into a bounded four-responsibility reconciliation model while explicitly separating liveness from exactly-once and distributed ownership claims.

readerTakeaway: Design durability as two contracts: preserve state, then separately define how live runtimes discover changed or resumed work, own retries and hand off to a claim/idempotency layer when exclusive execution matters.

supported: SQLite PRAGMA data_version is used as a coarse detector for writes through another connection.
Durable per-thread revisions identify changed loaded queues and change across insert, update and delete with migration backfill.
Created/resumed threads are reconciled separately, and per-thread watcher tasks retry unresolved wakeups on a fixed 10-second interval.
uncertain: How multiple runtimes coordinate after observing the same change
Appropriate backoff, fairness and load shedding at scale

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article is a general durable-work architecture analysis and does not depend on a first-party project.

decisionReason: The implementation provides mechanism-level evidence for discovery and retry, while the Research Object adds a reusable separation between persistence, reconciliation and stronger execution guarantees.
